title: Prove identity-pivot Schur dimension bounds; attain 4d (no κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR #4634 leaves open what changes when both leading blocks must be identities. This adds one self-contained package, `research/identity-pivot-schur/`, proving that for commuting binary idempotents with leading blocks `I_d` and Schur-commutator rank `2d`:

- `n >= L(d) = min_{t=0,...,d} max(3d+2t, 4d-3t) >= ceil(17d/5)`. In particular the unrestricted-pivot optimum `n=3d` is impossible.
- A new explicit construction attains `n=4d` for every `d>=2`, improving #4617's identity-pivot `5d` family.
- **For d=2, the exact minimum is n=8.** For general d, `4d` is optimal within the class where `H+H^2` is invertible, with H the leading block of PQ.

The proof specializes Nick Petalas's ordered factorization to `K=AB` and derives `BA=[[J,0],[J,J]]`, where `J=H+H^2`. Rank-nullity and the four joint-sector projectors give the lower bounds. A four-block change of basis supplies the upper bound. README Sections 1–3 contain the complete argument and a literal 8-by-8 witness.

**No new κ, header density, physical caller or supplier admission.** At this package's first publication the unrestricted identity-pivot minimum lay between L(d) and 4d. [Successor PR #4671](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4671) now closes that gap with the exact minimum n(H)=4d+nullity(H+H²) for every prescribed leading block H of PQ, hence 4d for all d>=2. Universal claims rest on the written proof, not extrapolation from samples.

## Task and overlap

Canonical base and submission refresh: `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`, priority revision 7, selected conditional κ=0.00302015. Head: `b79f90bc8d839a4998a40b10bcb437e87baa8397`.

Nearest predecessors: #4597 (`dfeb8ca7`, factorization), #4609 (`eb5ccf92`, scalar witness), #4617 (`96c01a21`, 5d family), #4634 (`9f053f70`, unrestricted 3d optimum and this open question). Full hashes and source paths are in TASK.json. All four heads were unchanged on the final live check.

The final overlap refresh covered 426 open PR bodies (14:27 UTC), 3,588 Discussion records (14:29 UTC), and every one of 5,862 in-scope local notes, with no coverage warnings. It located the credited open question and this claim, not a duplicate result. This is not a search of every diff, closed PR or unpublished result.

## Validation

Python 3.12.11 / macOS arm64, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/identity-pivot-schur
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/identity-pivot-schur --check-source-history
```

- Registered ordinary and optimized Python replays pass; checks use explicit exceptions.
- Direct full-matrix checks cover the literal witness, d=2..12, zero padding, all 2/48 admissible binary seeds of sizes 2/3, and a mixed singular-J fixture.
- Exhaustive identity-pivot commuting-idempotent domains contain 253 ordered pairs at (n,d)=(3,1) and 1,219 at (4,2); both factorizations and joint-sector identities pass.
- Eleven controls reject invalid premises, factor omissions, false sharpness and the invalid inference that a sharp rectangular product forces J invertible. The last control uses the credited #4617 scalar witness.
- All five committed files and source-history pins pass. Official export and integrity checks pass. The exported verifier passes with `-I -O -B`, no Git checkout and `PATH=/nonexistent`; all six export files, including its receipt, remain unchanged.
- The affected-package planner selects only `research/identity-pivot-schur`; the working tree is clean.

Pending predecessors are citations, not replay-time Git dependencies. The two attributed scalar control matrices are contained in the checker. No predecessor executable is imported.

No independent human or formal-kernel review is claimed. Lean, Docker and the selected scientific cold replay were not run. The separate selected baseline attempt stopped at an omitted sparse-checkout checkpoint; no baseline pass is claimed. Hosted CI is separate from these local results. The [Registered research packages run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39796568106) on exact head `b79f90bc8d839a4998a40b10bcb437e87baa8397` reports `action_required`: a maintainer must approve the fork workflow before it can run. No hosted replay pass is claimed.

Cinna Davis supplies the earlier BIT request/header setting. Predecessor AI disclosures and Apache-2.0 attribution are retained.

Prepared for **ssafwann** with substantial **OpenAI Codex (gpt-6-astra)** assistance, by one agent. No shared code, frozen evidence or selected frontier changes.

## Open next questions

The original singular-J dimension question is answered by [successor PR #4671](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4671): sharpness requires n>=4d+nullity(J), and the bound is attained for every H. The remaining complete-header counting question and its scope are recorded there and in [Discussion #4653](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4653). This PR retains the first proof, bounds, construction and verification artifact unchanged.
